non_blocking_notes: LQGovernance README covers agendas with attendance, per-document access control with deny-wins recusals, minutes draft/comment/Ed25519 signing, quorum-aware voting with signed certificates, tasks with evidence, audit chain and Docker/Caddy deployment. It does not explicitly state that documents are assembled against individual agenda items, nor that minutes pass a formal confirmation step that locks the meeting; the leaf's core is met in substance (meeting cycle + member-scoped material distribution + retained signed record), so this is noted rather than blocking.

The MIT text in the license API snapshot is the complete MIT license body (permission grant, notice retention, warranty disclaimer), with copyright 2026 held by an individual (Alexios van der Slikke-Kirillov) rather than the LegalQuants organization. Full-license and repository identity (id 1203202128, nwo LegalQuants/LQGovernance-OpenBoard, main branch) are consistent; the copyright-holder naming is not a licensing defect.

No open-core/paid-tier split is described for LQGovernance: the README states a single organization per deployment with per-board membership as the isolation boundary, and ships one Docker image under MIT. The 'community edition boundary' is therefore effectively the whole product, which is consistent with the open_source track.

LQGovernance is self-described as beta with documented security limitations (no application-level encryption at rest, audit chain not tamper-evident against app-server compromise, no external anchor). These are vendor-stated limits, not evidence problems, but could be summarised in the entry if readers might assume production hardening.

corporate-governance-platform.definitional_core: Partially verified. Open-source side: LQGovernance README body establishes a governed body with members, meetings with agendas and attendance that the vote tally consults, board materials with a single member-scoped access model (membership OR explicit grant MINUS explicit deny, deny-wins recusals), minutes drafted/commented/signed with per-user Ed25519 keys, voting with quorum/approval thresholds and signed certificates, tasks with evidence and review, and an HMAC audit chain — i.e. agenda, meeting, member-scoped material distribution and retained governance record. Commercial side: Diligent's /products/boards snapshot is truncated before the product body (nav, hero SVG and one testimonial only), so its meeting-cycle core is not demonstrated in the cited evidence.
corporate-governance-platform.saas_service_form: Verified for the open-source entry: a continuously running, multi-user, self-hosted web application (React SPA + Express API + PostgreSQL + Socket.IO) delivered as a single Docker image with Compose, Caddy/HTTPS and DEPLOY.md — a software service, not a script, SDK or static template. Diligent is a vendor-hosted commercial web product; only its existence and board-governance positioning are evidenced, given the snapshot truncation.
